title: Parity decision: SF counters wrap at 255 in C (uint8_t) vs unbounded ints in Python port
description: Found by reviewer pass 1 on bead project-LICHEN-zrh2.7 (Python adaptive-SF port, gradient.py). C lichen_gradient_sf_update (gradient.c) uses uint8_t upgrade_count/downgrade_count: after 255 consecutive same-side samples the counter wraps to 0, suppressing the step-4 upgrade for UPGRADE_COUNT_THRESHOLD (3) samples; the Python port (python/src/lichen/gradient.py GradientTable.sf_update) uses unbounded ints so the count keeps rising and the step-4 gate (upgrade_count >= 3) never suppresses. Deliberate decision needed: (a) treat the C wrap as accidental (probable - a 255-sample consecutive-same-side run overflows) and change C to saturate at 255 (uint8 clamp, matches Python), or (b) reproduce the wrap in Python for exact parity. Sibling zrh2.8 (unit tests for adaptive SF, both C and Python) should pin whichever semantics are chosen. Python behavior today: unbounded (matches the documented consecutive-samples semantics, not the C storage quirk).
